summary: Albert Fish abducted and murdered children in and around New York City in the 1920s, cannibalising Grace Budd, and was caught in 1934 after taunting her family by letter; he was executed in 1936.

evidence.note: first abduction and killing, a boy on Staten Island in 1924
mobs attack suspected child snatchers after the Gaffney abduction
kidnapping craze of the early 1930s and the Lindbergh case tied to these crimes
detective planted false leads with a gossip columnist to keep the case alive
stationery traced to a rooming house leads to the arrest
psychiatrist Wertham examines Fish for the court and finds him insane
childhood in an orphanage after his father's death
execution in the electric chair in January 1936
modern collector who owns the original letter, used for reaches_present

notes: No theme for serial killers or mental illness; child-abuse chosen as primary for the child murders. A long segment on the guest's descent from Fish and a modern collector of his letter drives reaches_present. Transcript puts the arrest in 1934; real arrest was December 1934, consistent.
